mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 2.5% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 YoY growth < -2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods when UNRATE > 4.5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a broad-based contraction in economic activity, which depresses earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both INDPRO and HOUST decline by more than 1% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp reduction in the federal funds rate below 1% during a recessionary regime signals an aggressive monetary easing, which boosts risk appetite and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS < 1% and UNRATE > 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A strong acceleration in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1 YoY growth > 3%) coincident with stable inflation (CPIAUCSL YoY growth within 1.5-2.5%) signals robust demand growth without inflationary pressure, which supports earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY growth > 3% AND CPIAUCSL YoY growth in [1.5,2.5]%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when GDPC1 YoY > 3% and CPIAUCSL YoY in [1.5,2.5]%.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) by more than 1% month-over-month signals labor market strength, which boosts consumer spending and corporate hiring, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS increases by more than 1% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous recovery in both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 0.5% month-over-month after a prior two-month decline signals a rebound in supply capacity, which improves earnings and triggers positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO +0.5% MoM AND HOUST +0.5% MoM after two months of decline
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when INDPRO and HOUST both rebound by >0.5% MoM after two months of decline.
